label: rem:chi-v21-hoefsmit-matrix-derivation
title: $V_{(2,1)}$ Hoefsmit $2\times 2$ matrix derivation: scalar trace + Hecke-quadratic identities + Laurent decomposition of the closed form $-(q^4+1)(q^2-1)/(4q^3)$
html:
V_(2,1) Hoefsmit 2\times2 matrix derivation — partial closure.

V_{(2,1)} provides the 2-dimensional Hoefsmit irrep of H_3(q). Unlike V_{(3)} and V_{(1,1,1)} (1-d, scalar arithmetic), V_{(2,1)} requires the full 2\times2 matrix representation:

  \sigma_0 \mapsto \begin{pmatrix} q & 0 \\ 0 & -q^{-1} \end{pmatrix},
  \quad
  \sigma_1 \mapsto \begin{pmatrix} d_1 & b \\ b & d_2 \end{pmatrix}

with d_1 = -q^{-1}/(q^2+1), d_2 = q^3/(q^2+1), b^2 = d_1 d_2 + 1.

Uniqueness of the diagonal assignment (d_1, d_2). With \sigma_0 = \mathrm{diag}(q, -q^{-1}) fixed as above, the braid relation \sigma_0 \sigma_1 \sigma_0 = \sigma_1 \sigma_0 \sigma_1 admits the unique diagonal assignment (d_1, d_2) shown (up to the sign of b, and the degenerate b = 0). The transposed pair (d_2, d_1) satisfies the Hecke quadratic relation, has the same trace q - q^{-1} and determinant -1, and yields the same b^2 — all four of those quantities are symmetric in d_1, d_2 — yet fails the braid relation and therefore does not define a representation of B_3. At q = 1 the representation reduces to the classical Young orthogonal matrix s_2 = \begin{pmatrix} -1/2 & \sqrt3/2 \\ \sqrt3/2 & 1/2 \end{pmatrix} on the two-dimensional irreducible representation of S_3.

  \chi_{(2,1)}(\mathcal{B}_n) - \chi_{(2,1)}(\mathcal{B}_p)
   = -\frac{(q^4 + 1)(q^2 - 1)}{4 q^3}.

Proved identities

q + (-q^{-1}) = q - q^{-1}
d_1 + d_2 = q - q^{-1}
factored \leftrightarrow polynomial form
explicit Laurent: -q^3/4 + q/4 - q^{-1}/4 + q^{-3}/4
numerical cross-checks at q = 1, 2
\sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 = \sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_1, generic b with b^2 = d_1d_2+1
the 11-crossing matrix-product trace difference

Laurent decomposition and the ε^k growth

Unlike V_(3) where the inverse-Laurent has only one term (q^{-1}/4, giving bounded oscillation), V_(2,1) has two inverse terms (q^{-1}/4 and q^{-3}/4), and the q^{-3}/4 term has \binom{k+2}{2} growth \sim k^2/2. This matches the observed asymptotic \sim k(k+3)/2 for the V_(2,1) coefficients.

The matrix-product trace identity

The full matrix-product trace identity is proved:

  1. The Hoefsmit matrices \sigma_0, \sigma_1 are taken as real 2 \times 2 matrices.
  2. The non-invariance under the diagonal transposition d_1 \leftrightarrow d_2 is established: the transposed matrices yield a trace difference \chi_{(2,1)}(\mathcal{B}_n) - \chi_{(2,1)}(\mathcal{B}_p) larger than the closed form above by a factor of (q^4+q^2+1)/q^2 = q^2 + 1 + q^{-2}, verified symbolically and at the rational points q = 2, q = 3/2, and q = 1.1099. Although b^2, the trace, and the determinant are symmetric under the swap, the braid relation couples \sigma_0 to \sigma_1 and excludes the transposed pair.
  3. The explicit 11-crossing word orders for \beta_p and \beta_n enter the proof directly.

Only even powers of b reach the trace. Each index-1 factor is symmetric with off-diagonal b, and a path from a diagonal slot back to itself takes an even number of off-diagonal steps. Odd powers do occur — b^3 appears 20 times in the normalised matrix — but only in the off-diagonal entries, which the trace discards.
